candidates.changed_node: removed the whole modulator product CS_RANK(MAX(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), 0)) * CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42)), replacing it with a single CS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 21)) risk leg, and dropped the redundant CS_DEMEAN wrapper - drops $leverage, $volume, $high, $low and the 0 clip constant
candidates.rationale: Parent is quality minus a two-part turbulence modulator: rising leverage times volume/range comovement. Both halves proxy the same thing, so they collapse into one realised-vol penalty. Cost drops from 5 fields + 1 free constant + depth 5 to 2 fields + 0 constants + depth 4; the CS_DEMEAN wrapper goes too, since it is a monotone shift of CS_RANK and rank-identical. IC floor is 0.00902 and this chassis is already measured: the same spread at window 42 scored mean IC 0.01257 (t 3.71, coverage 0.976) in this run and cleared every gate, and at window 10 it scored 0.01348 before that member was evicted, so window 21 lands around 0.013 with wide margin. Structurally free: the only archive user of TS_STD($return, 21) is the evicted 26f2d231, and TS_STD($return, 21) is a 3-node block in any case, while Alpha101 uses stddev windows of 20 and below, so nothing shares 4 nodes. Keeping the corr kernel was not on offer: TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42) is the parent's own 6-node subtree, window 15 is the live sibling a12e85f4, and the free windows drew correlation rejects (105 at 0.867, 30 at 0.801). Window 21 also runs faster than the 42-day variant's 40.6-day half-life, so it competes in a different half-life niche rather than against a factor that already lost one.

candidates.changed_node: removed the CS_ZSCORE(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)) scaler and the TS_MEAN($open, 42) price normaliser around ($high - $low), plus the CS_DEMEAN wrapper - drops $leverage and $open, and the range is now scaled by correlating it with $return
candidates.rationale: Parent is quality minus (z-scored leverage growth x intraday range relative to price). The range term is what survives; the two things attached to it go. Fields 5 -> 4, depth 6 -> 5, CS_DEMEAN dropped as rank-identical. The leverage scaler cannot be kept in any form: every wrapper around TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) - CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE, ABS, MAX(.,0) - is already a 4-node live-archive block including this parent's own, and the bare roe-minus-leverage-delta spread measured rho 0.920 against 4cf4ee72. The price normaliser cannot be kept either: dropping only the leverage leg leaves a range-over-price rank, which measured rho 0.824 against the live CS_RANK($roe) - TS_RANK($high - $low, 10), and the parent's own ($high - $low) / (TS_MEAN($open, 42) + 1e-8) is a 9-node subtree. So the range is scaled by pairing it with $return inside a correlation instead: how tightly the day's move tracks the day's range is the same trading-wide-under-stress signal in one node, and the $return basis is what decorrelates it from the volume-vs-range corr legs. Evidence: this exact chassis at window 15 was scored in this run at mean IC 0.00761 and cleared correlation, archive_subtree and coverage, against a 0.00652 floor; corr legs in this archive strengthen with window (0.0070 at 21, 0.0078 at 63), so 42 is the safer horizon. Structurally free: the only archive user of TS_CORR($return, $high - $low, w) is ca6d1041 at w = 21 and it is evicted, while every live 42-day corr leg uses $volume.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: SIMPLIFY. Each expression below was flagged as more complex than it needs
to be. Return a simpler expression that keeps the same idea.

Simpler means strictly fewer distinct fields, fewer free constants, or less
depth. The simplification is accepted only if it also keeps at least
80% of the parent's fit-window |IC|, so do not remove the component
doing the work. Put the parent's id in `parent_ids` and name what you removed in
`changed_node`.
